intro: Fellow: an employee management app, and the DevOps pipeline that ships it.
slides-open: Fellow covers people, departments, leave, attendance and holidays for a small company.
The stack: React and FastAPI, tested, containerised, deployed to Kubernetes and monitored.
readme: The README documents the whole project: features, architecture, setup and operations.
Features: each area of the app and the business rules it enforces.
Architecture: the ingress sends / to the React frontend and /api to the FastAPI backend.
Delivery: tests, image build, Trivy scan, push to GHCR, then Argo CD deploys from Git.
The tech stack, layer by layer.
app-tour: The dashboard shows live numbers from the FastAPI backend, which queries PostgreSQL.
The sidebar collapses to an icon rail, and the choice is remembered in the browser.
Employees can be searched and filtered, and every page has its own URL.
A profile shows personal and job details, leave balances and monthly attendance.
Approving a leave request updates the request and the employee's balance through the API.
Checking in and out uses the server's clock, so the time cannot be changed from the browser.
Light and dark themes are both supported.
slides-arch: Architecture: browser, ingress, frontend and backend pods, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana and Argo CD.
codebase: One repository holds the app, the pipeline, the infrastructure and the docs.
The backend is split into FastAPI routers, one file per resource.
Routers validate input with Pydantic schemas and use SQLAlchemy to talk to PostgreSQL.
The Helm chart templates describe every Kubernetes object the app needs.
api-docs: FastAPI generates this interactive OpenAPI documentation automatically, at /docs.
Every endpoint is listed with its method, path, parameters and response schema.
Try it out: GET /api/employees/12 returns that employee as JSON, with status 200.
The response: status 200 with the employee as JSON, plus the matching curl command.
Next, an invalid update: PUT with the email set to null.
The API rejects it with status 422 and a clear message: email cannot be null.
The Schemas section lists every request and response model, defined with Pydantic.
slides-ci: Every push to main runs the pipeline: test, build, scan, publish, promote and sync.
ci-push: A real change is committed and pushed to main from the terminal.
The push triggers the GitHub Actions workflow.
ci-run: pytest and the frontend build run first; a failing test stops the pipeline (sped up 8x).
Both Docker images are built and scanned by Trivy, which fails the build on HIGH or CRITICAL CVEs.
Images are pushed to GitHub Container Registry, tagged with the commit SHA.
The last job commits the new image tag to Git for the staging environment.
Both images are listed in GitHub Container Registry.
argocd: Argo CD watches the Git repository and deploys that commit to the staging namespace.
Synced means the cluster matches Git; Healthy means every resource is running.
card-tf: Part 4: infrastructure as code with Terraform.
slides-tf: Terraform defines the VPC, subnets, NAT gateway, an optional EKS cluster and the kind cluster.
terraform: terraform plan compares the code with what exists and shows what would change.
The outputs list the IDs of the VPC, subnets and NAT gateway created in LocalStack.
The subnets exist in the emulated AWS API: two public and two private, across two zones.
Setting create_eks=true plans the EKS cluster, IAM roles and node group from the same code.
slides-k8s: One Helm chart deploys both environments: dev with Helm, staging with Argo CD.
kubernetes: The cluster has three nodes: one control plane and two workers.
Backend and frontend run two replicas each behind ClusterIP services; the ingress routes traffic.
helm list shows the releases for the app and for monitoring.
A load generator sends traffic to the backend while the HPA watches CPU (sped up 6x).
CPU goes above the 60% target, so the HPA scales the backend from 2 to 6 pods.
slides-obs: Prometheus collects the metrics and Grafana turns them into a dashboard.
metrics: The backend exposes Prometheus metrics at /metrics: request counts by endpoint, method and status.
The PUT 4xx counter is the invalid request sent from the API docs a moment ago.
observability: Prometheus scrapes every backend pod every 15 seconds, and all targets are UP.
This Grafana dashboard ships inside the Helm chart.
During the load test, request rate, latency and CPU per pod all rise.
The autoscaling panel shows the replicas going up to 6.
slides-ts: Real problems found and fixed while building the project.
troubleshooting: Lab 1: a deployment points at an image tag that does not exist.
The pod cannot start: ErrImagePull, then ImagePullBackOff.
The events explain why: the image was not found in the registry.
Lab 2: a Service whose selector matches no pods has no endpoints.
Patching the selector to the real pod label brings the endpoints back.
slides-end: Key learnings: gate early, let Git drive deployments, and measure before scaling.
Code, docs, slides and this video are all in the GitHub repository.
